neighbours.label: 'like' in 'looks (something) like this:' introducing a shown example
fire:
Your config file should look something like this:
port = 8080
After the update, the output of the command looks like this: OK 200 done.
A typical entry in the log looks like this: [INFO] server started.
The final directory layout should look roughly like this: src, tests, docs.
In the end, the request header looked something like this: Accept: text/html.
Once rendered, the table will look like this: name, age, city.
Each line in the CSV export looks like this: 42,blue,2020-01-01.
The generated URL will look like this: https://example.com/item/42.
quiet: Many developers like this config file because it is short and readable.
After the update, I really like the output of the command much better.
A typical user would like the log to be shorter and easier to read.
The team did not like the final directory layout and changed it again.
In the end, the request header was rewritten to accept plain text.
Once rendered, the table is sent to the printer in the main office.
Each line in the CSV export is checked against the schema before upload.
The generated URL is stored in the database for later reuse.
